name: Camber Sands
text: Camber Sands is a beach in East Sussex, England, in the village of Camber, near Rye. It is the only sand dune system in East Sussex. Located east of the estuary of the River Rother at Rye Bay, it stretches 3 miles (4.8 km) to just beyond the Kent border, where shingle (pebbles) take over again.

depictions.name: Camber Sands
depictions.text: The Camber Sands, also known as Cleofa Sands during the Anglo-Saxon period, is a beach in Sussex, England, east of the Seven Sisters cliffs. It is the only sand dune system in the county, and unlike most of the beaches in England, Camber Sands is made purely of sand rather than shredding pebbles. During the 870s, the beach was visited by the Viking Eivor Varinsdottir during her time in the shire.
